content: GM delivered a clean 2Q beat and raised 2026 EBIT guidance, while offering positive preliminary commentary on the 2027 outlook. Software and non-auto (Defense and ESS) are pivotal to drive the next leg of multiple re-rating, in our view.
- Beat & Raise: 2Q EBIT beat, driven by strong GMNA performance. Guidance raised by $500m at the midpoint ($14-$16bn vs. MSe of $15.4bn).
2027 Bridge: Management's first directional outlook points to ~$16bn of adj. EBIT, based on our estimates.
■ Software inflection: Deferred revenue is on track to hit $7.5bn by year-end, driving double-digit growth in realized revenue in 2027 at a 70% gross margin.
Non-auto optionality: Defense revenue nearing $700mn with positive EBIT targeted for '26; sodium-ion battery investment adds long-term optionality.
EV overhang cleared: $2.3bn of EV charges closes out a multi-quarter business review, removing lingering uncertainty on capital return cadence/optionality.
Key Takeaways from Earnings - see our quick take here.

Clean beat, raised guide. GM delivered a strong beat led by North America where EBIT came in 8% above our expectations due to stronger pricing and cost management, including EV-loss and warranty improvements. As for the full year guide, GM increased 2026 EBIT guidance by $500m at the midpoint ($14-$16bn range), driven by better pricing (up ~0.5% vs. previously "flat to up 0.5%") and improved warranty costs ($1-$1.5bn Y/Y tailwind vs. ~$1bn tailwind previously).

Directional outlook calls for growth in 2027. Management provided its first high level outlook for 2027, signaling growth in revenue, EBIT, and FCF, driven by improving EV profitability, digital revenue, incremental warranty savings, strengthened pricing power on next-gen Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra pickups, and increased full-size SUV supply to meet US demand. We expect this to be partially offset by the full year impact of higher commodity/DRAM costs and incremental tariff headwinds (due to the non-recurrence of the IEEPA refund recognized in 2026). As a result, we forecast GM to generate ~$16bn of adj. EBIT in 2027 (Exhibit 1). Our framework to contextualize some of the moving pieces for the 2027 bridge is as follows. Tailwinds: (i) $0.5-$1bn improvement in EV losses (vs. $1-$1.5bn improvement in 2026), (ii) $0.5bn-$1bn improvement in warranty costs (vs. $1-$1.5bn improvement in 2026), (iii) $350-$750mn improvement from volume/price. Software and Services is an underappreciated growth driver. GM is positioning the digital services vector as an increasingly material and less-cyclical earnings engine, with 1mn new digital subscriptions expected in 2026 supporting more than $3bn of recognized revenue. In 2Q, deferred revenue reached $6.3bn (+50% y/y) and is on track to reach $7.5bn by year-end, supporting double-digit realized revenue growth in 2027 at ~70% gross margins. We expect to see longer-term software and services growth driven by 1) increasing availability of Super Cruise across additional vehicle models/trims, 2) scaling high-margin subscription revenue following the included service period, and 3) increasing ARPU as functionality improves (i.e. eyes off). We believe GM's software and services business has the potential to drive a significant re-rating in the shares as the company accretes high margin revenue through the P&L, and continues to add disclosure around the outlook for this business.

Other areas of non-auto growth. We have previously written about how non-auto is becoming a core focus for investors, and see GM's Defense and Energy verticals as key opportunities for margin expansion and topline growth. In Defense, management expects 2026 revenue to approach $700mn (still <1% of total revenue) and the business to reach positive EBIT, while targeting more than 30% annual revenue growth over the next several years and double-digit margins. Separately, management's commentary on the sodium-ion battery opportunity corroborates our view that the technology provides potential cost advantages vs LFP, abundant raw materials, broad temperature performance, and lower cooling and maintenance requirements. We believe the Peak Energy partnership, which provides exposure with a capital-light approach, is consistent with management's broader execution strategy of preserving capital efficiency while maintaining strategic optionality. While we recognize the value of establishing a strategic foothold in the energy storage market, as well as the potential for the technology to extend into vehicle applications over time, production may not scale until the end of the decade,

Finalized EV-related charges removes any remaining capital return uncertainty. GM substantially completed the review of its EV business, resulting in an incremental \$2.3bn charge in the quarter. While the company has been clear about its commitment to its capital return program, we believe the conclusion of their EV business review helps remove a lingering overhang around the capital return opportunity at GM (i.e. investors concerned that capital return may be negatively impacted by future cash charges).

How our estimates are changing (Exhibit 2). Our estimates are broadly unchanged as we were already modeling towards the high end of the company's prior guidance range on the view that the company had several levers to drive upside to its guidance (as seen with this earnings print). We believe further upside to estimates could come from (i) an improved commodity cost outlook, (ii) a favorable pricing environment, even as GM approaches its truck changeover at the end of the year, (iii) further warranty improvement, or (iv) additional cost rationalization measures. Our PT increases to $101, primarily driven by a lower share count.

At the macro level, GM will benefit from 1) reduced policy uncertainty, 2) the sunsetting of EV tax credits, and 3) expected rate cuts to help affordability in 2H26. Beyond the favorable macro setup, GM has demonstrated strong execution with industry-leading US inventory and incentive discipline and tariff mitigation efforts via supply chain re-alignment (\$4bn investment in US) and go to market strategies, as well as a marked turnaround in International. Despite our expectation for moderating 2026 US SAAR, we expect GM to manage through with an appropriately re-aligned capital allocation strategy and refreshed product lineup highlighting strength in GM's core ICE trucks and SUVs.
View descriptions of Risk Rewards Themes here

Our $138 DCF-derived bull case implies ~9.1x our bull case 2026 EPS of $15.09 (~1.8x turn premium to base case). Beyond stronger earnings growth in the near-term, we believe multiple expansion will originate from GM's ability to advance personal autonomous driving (Super Cruise) and software and services offering. DCF assumptions include +2.4%/+3.1% revenue/EBIT (ex-GMF) CAGR to 2035 discounted at a 11.2% WACC and a 7.5x exit FCF multiple.

Our DCF-derived $101 price target implies ~7.3x 2026 EPS of $13.93, which is a ~1.2x premium to current trading levels. DCF assumptions include +1.6%/+0.3% revenue/EBIT (ex-GMF) CAGR to 2035 discounted at a 11.2% WACC and a 4.0x exit FCF multiple. Our 2026 EPS estimates is above consensus.

Our $55 DCF-derived bear case implies ~4.7x our bear case 2026 EPS of $11.83 (~2.6x turn discount to base case and in line with 1st quartile of historical multiple). DCF assumptions include -2.0%/-5.6% revenue/EBIT (ex-GMF) CAGR to 2035 discounted at a 11.2% WACC and a 3.5x exit FCF multiple.
